stages.title: Reading and writing fundamentals
explain: French spelling keeps history. Many letters are written but not said: the s of "petits", the nt of "ils mangent". These letters often show grammar, such as plural or verb person.

Learn the main sound spellings: "ou" says /u/, "eau" and "au" say /o/, "oi" says /wa/, "ai" says /e/ or /ɛ/, and "ch" says /sh/. Capital letters are not used for days, months or languages: "lundi", "janvier", "français".

gq.why: The spelling eau stands for the single sound /o/.

gq.q: Why is the s in "petits" written if it is silent?
gq.why: Silent endings often carry grammar information.

panel.q: Which sentence is written correctly?
panel.why: In French, names of languages are written with a small letter.

panel.q: Why do "il mange" and "ils mangent" sound the same?
o: They are the same word written twice
panel.why: Plural verb endings in -ent are not pronounced.

panel.q: A pupil writes "les chat". What does the error show?
o: The plural is not marked on the article and noun
The verb is missing, so the sentence has no real meaning
panel.why: Both the article and the noun need plural marks: les chats.

points.ask: How do I read letter groups?

teach.model: French spelling has many silent letters. They often show grammar, like the s of plural nouns. Some letter groups make one sound, like eau for /o/ and ou for /u/.

stages.hook: When you read "ils mangent", how many sounds do you hear at the end? And why are so many letters written?
stages.mnemonic: Written letters carry grammar even when the ear hears nothing.

trip.prompt: Find the section on silent letters and note one reason the spelling stayed while the sound changed.

stages.title: Basic sentence construction
explain: A basic French sentence is subject, verb, object: "Marie mange une pomme". The adjective usually follows the noun: "une voiture rouge", but short common adjectives like grand, petit, bon, beau and jeune usually come before: "un grand arbre".
To say no, put "ne" before the verb and "pas" after it: "Je ne mange pas". In speech, "ne" often disappears: "Je mange pas". Before a vowel, ne becomes n': "Il n'aime pas".

gq.q: How do you make "Je mange" negative?
gq.why: Ne goes before the verb and pas after it.

gq.q: Why is it "un petit chien" but "un chien noir"?
o: Petit is a short common adjective that goes before the noun
Noir is a plural adjective, so it has to be placed after the noun
gq.why: Short common adjectives such as petit come before; colours follow.

panel.q: Why does ne become n' in "Il n'aime pas"?
o: Ne drops its vowel before a vowel sound
It is a typing mistake that has become common
panel.why: Elision happens before a vowel sound.

panel.q: In spoken French "Je sais pas" is common. What does it show?
o: Ne is often dropped in speech
Pas is optional and can be dropped in speech
panel.why: Colloquial speech often omits ne, while writing keeps it.

panel.q: In "Je ne mange pas de viande", why is it "de" and not "de la"?
o: After a negation, de replaces de la
Because pas is followed by an article
Because de la is only for questions
panel.why: After a negation, the indefinite and partitive articles (un, une, du, de la, des) become de.

teach.model: A French sentence goes subject, verb, object. Colours follow the noun, but short adjectives like grand and petit go before it. For no, put ne before the verb and pas after it.

stages.hook: In English we say "a red car". In French, where does the colour go?
stages.mnemonic: Ne ... pas: the verb sits in a sandwich.

trip.prompt: Find the word-order section and note where adjectives usually sit compared with English.

stages.title: Common verbs
explain: The most common verbs are irregular: être (je suis, tu es, il est, nous sommes, vous êtes, ils sont) and avoir (j'ai, tu as, il a, nous avons, vous avez, ils ont). Also aller (to go): je vais, tu vas, il va, nous allons, vous allez, ils vont.
Faire (to do, make): je fais, tu fais, il fait, nous faisons, vous faites, ils font. Use aller + infinitive for the near future: "Je vais manger".

gq.q: Choose the correct form: Nous ___ à Paris.
gq.why: Nous goes with the form allons.

gq.q: Why is "ils ont" different from "ils sont"?
o: They are different verbs, avoir and être
They are the same verb written in two different ways
gq.why: Ont is from avoir (have) and sont from être (be).

panel.q: How do you say "I am going to eat"?
panel.why: Aller plus an infinitive gives the near future.

panel.q: In "vous faites" the ending is -tes. What does that show?
panel.why: Faire does not follow the regular pattern.

panel.q: Why are the most frequent verbs usually irregular?
o: They were used so often that they kept old forms
They are new words that have not been regularised yet
panel.why: Frequent words resist change and keep irregular forms.

points.ask: How do I say going to?

teach.model: Être means to be, avoir means to have, aller means to go and faire means to do. They are irregular, so learn each form. For example je suis, j'ai, je vais, je fais.

stages.hook: In French "I am" is "je suis" and "I have" is "j'ai". What do the most common verbs look like?
stages.mnemonic: Être, avoir, aller, faire: the four verbs you must know by heart.

trip.prompt: Find the forms of être and avoir and write the nous form of each.

stages.title: Nouns, pronouns and modifiers
explain: Use "le" with masculine singular, "la" with feminine singular and "les" with all plurals. Add -s to make most plurals. Words with -eau take -x: "un bateau, des bateaux". Words with -al change to -aux: "un journal, des journaux".

Subject pronouns are je, tu, il, elle, on, nous, vous, ils, elles. "On" is very common and means "we" or "one". Possessives agree with the noun they describe: "son livre" can mean his book or her book.

gq.q: What is the plural of "un journal"?
Why does "son livre" not show whether the owner is a man or a woman?
o: Son agrees with the noun owned, not the owner
Son is only used for men, so the owner is always male
gq.why: French possessives agree with the thing possessed.

panel.q: Why do we say "ce livre" but "cet arbre"?
o: Cet is used before a vowel sound
Arbre is a feminine noun, so cet is needed
panel.why: Ce becomes cet before a masculine word starting with a vowel.

panel.q: What does "on" often replace in spoken French?
panel.why: On is frequently used instead of nous, with a singular verb.

panel.q: Why can a learner say "sa mère" for both "his mother" and "her mother"?
o: Sa agrees with the noun mère, which is feminine
Sa agrees with the owner, who is always a woman
panel.why: The possessive follows the gender of the noun owned.

teach.model: Use le, la or les with the gender and number of the noun. Add -s for most plurals, -x for -eau and -aux for -al. On is a common word for we.

stages.hook: In French, "le", "la" and "les" all mean "the". How do you pick the right one?
stages.mnemonic: Le, la, les: masculine, feminine, many.

trip.prompt: Find the section on gender or number and note one rule for making a plural.

stages.title: Questions and responses
explain: There are three ways. Intonation: "Tu aimes la pizza?" Add "Est-ce que": "Est-ce que tu aimes la pizza?" Or invert verb and subject: "Aimes-tu la pizza?" The first is spoken and informal, the last is more formal.

Question words: qui (who), que or quoi (what), où (where), quand (when), pourquoi (why), comment (how), combien (how much). To answer "Why?" start with "Parce que". Yes is oui, but to contradict a negative question say "si".

gq.q: Which is the most formal way to ask a question?
o: Rising voice: Tu aimes la pizza?
Est-ce que tu aimes la pizza?
gq.why: Inversion is common in writing and formal speech.

gq.q: Someone asks "Tu n'aimes pas le thé?" and you like tea. What do you say?
gq.why: Si is used to contradict a negative question.

panel.q: Why does "Où habites-tu?" have a hyphen?
o: The verb and pronoun are inverted and joined
The hyphen shows that the verb is in the plural form
panel.why: A hyphen links an inverted verb and subject.

panel.q: Which answer fits "Pourquoi tu pleures?"
o: Quand je pleure, mais pas très souvent
panel.why: Pourquoi is answered with parce que.

panel.q: Why can intonation alone make a question in French?
o: French word order stays the same, only the voice rises
French has no question marks, so the voice must show it
panel.why: Spoken French often uses a rising pitch with the statement order.

teach.model: In French you can ask by raising your voice, by adding est-ce que or by inverting verb and subject. Use qui, où, quand, pourquoi, comment and combien to ask for information. Answer why with parce que.

stages.hook: How many ways can you ask "Do you like pizza?" in French?
stages.mnemonic: Qui, quoi, où, quand, comment: the five key question words.

trip.prompt: Find the section on questions and note the three ways of asking one in French.

stages.title: Describing people and places
explain: Adjectives agree with the noun. For a girl we usually add e: "grand" becomes "grande", "petit" becomes "petite", "content" becomes "contente". For plural add s: "grands", "grandes".
Some adjectives do not add e because they already end in e: "jeune", "rouge", "facile". To describe places use "il y a" (there is): "Il y a un parc près de ma maison." Add "très" for very.
sentences: There is a park near here.

gq.q: Choose the correct form: Elle est ___
gq.why: Elle is feminine singular, so petit becomes petite.

gq.q: Why does "jeune" not change in "une jeune fille"?
o: It is a plural form, so it never changes
gq.why: Adjectives ending in -e have the same masculine and feminine form.

panel.q: What is the feminine form of "beau"?
panel.why: Beau has an irregular feminine, belle.

panel.q: Why is it "un bel homme"?
o: Bel is used before a masculine noun starting with a vowel sound
Homme is a feminine noun, and bel is the feminine form of the word beau
panel.why: Beau becomes bel before a vowel or silent h.

panel.q: Why is gentil pronounced differently from gentille?
o: The final consonant sound appears in the feminine
They are spelled the same way, so they sound the same
The e is silent in gentil
panel.why: Feminine forms add a pronounced consonant (gentil / gentij).

points.ask: How do I describe a place?

teach.model: Adjectives agree with the noun in French. Add e for feminine and s for plural. Adjectives ending in e do not change for feminine. Use il y a to say what is in a place.

stages.hook: How do you describe a tall girl and a tall boy? Does "grand" change?
stages.mnemonic: Add e for girls, add s for many.

trip.prompt: Find the section on agreement and note how an adjective can change with the noun it describes.

stages.title: Time, dates and daily routines
explain: To say the time use "Il est ... heure(s)": "Il est trois heures." For half past say "et demie", for quarter past say "et quart", and quarter to say "moins le quart". Midday is midi and midnight is minuit.

Days: lundi, mardi, mercredi, jeudi, vendredi, samedi, dimanche. The date is: "le 5 mai". Say "le premier mai" for the first. Daily routine verbs are reflexive: "Je me lève" (I get up), "Je me couche" (I go to bed).

o: Il est trois heures et demie
Il est trois heures moins demie
Il est trois et demi heures

gq.q: Why is it "le premier mai" but "le deux mai"?
o: The first of the month uses an ordinal
The first is plural, so it needs a special number
gq.why: French uses an ordinal for the first and cardinal numbers for the rest.

panel.q: What does "Je me lève" show about French routines?
o: Reflexive verbs show actions done to oneself
They are past tenses used for morning routines
panel.why: Reflexive verbs have a pronoun like me.

panel.q: How is "Il est midi et quart" translated?
o: It is quarter to twelve at noon
panel.why: Et quart means quarter past.

panel.q: Why are days and months not capitalised in French?
o: French capitalises only names and sentence starts
They are unimportant words, so they are written small
panel.why: Days and months are common nouns in French.

points.ask: How do I say the time?
How do I say I get up?

teach.model: Say Il est plus the hour. Add et quart, et demie or moins le quart. Days of the week are written with small letters. For routine actions use reflexive verbs like je me lève.

sources: Date and time notation in France
stages.hook: What time is it? How do you give a date in French?
stages.mnemonic: Days start on lundi, which echoes lune, the moon.

trip.wiki: Date and time notation in France
trip.prompt: Find how dates and times are written in France and note one difference from your own country.

stages.title: Food and shopping
explain: Say "Je voudrais une baguette, s'il vous plaît." The word "voudrais" is polite. Ask the price with "C'est combien?" or "Ça coûte combien?"

Use the partitive "du, de la, des" for unspecified quantity: "Je mange du pain, de la viande, des légumes." After a quantity word use de: "un kilo de pommes". Money in France is the euro. Shops include la boulangerie, la boucherie and le marché.

gq.why: Du is the partitive for masculine nouns.

gq.q: Why is it "un kilo de pommes" and not "un kilo des pommes"?
o: After a quantity, de is used
Pommes is singular, so des cannot be used with it
gq.why: Quantity expressions are followed by de alone.

panel.q: Why do customers say "Je voudrais" instead of "Je veux"?
o: It is the past tense of the verb vouloir
panel.why: Voudrais is the conditional and sounds courteous.

panel.q: In a shop, which greeting is expected on entering?
panel.why: Greeting the shopkeeper with bonjour is a basic courtesy.

panel.q: Why do we say "Je mange du pain" when English says just "I eat bread"?
o: French uses the partitive article for an unspecified amount
English has no word for bread, so French needs du to name it
panel.why: French normally needs du, de la or des where English uses no article.

points.ask: How do I ask the price?
How do I say some bread?

teach.model: In a shop say Bonjour and Je voudrais to order politely. Ask C'est combien? for the price. Use du, de la or des for some of something. Use de after quantities.

stages.hook: You are in a French bakery. How do you ask for bread and pay?
stages.mnemonic: Du pain, de la soupe, des pommes: some of it.

trip.prompt: Find one product that a French bakery sells besides bread.

stages.title: Everyday conversations
explain: A typical conversation starts with a greeting, then "Ça va?" The answer can be "Ça va bien", "Pas mal" or "Comme ci, comme ça". After that you can ask "Et toi?" or ask about plans.
To make a plan say "On y va?" (shall we go?) and "D'accord" (agreed). To end say "À bientôt" (see you soon), "À demain" (see you tomorrow) or "Bonne journée" (have a good day).
sentences: I am sorry, I am late.

gq.q: A friend asks "Ça va?" What is a good reply?
o: Au revoir, à demain, mon ami
gq.why: The reply and the return question keep the chat going.

gq.q: Why is "Et toi?" used with a friend and "Et vous?" with a stranger?
o: Toi is plural and vous is singular here
gq.why: The form depends on the relationship.

panel.q: What does "D'accord" show in a conversation?
panel.why: D'accord means OK or agreed.

panel.q: Why is "Bonne journée" said when leaving?
o: It wishes the other person a good day
It greets someone you have just met in the morning
panel.why: It is a standard way to close a conversation.

panel.q: What makes a conversation sound polite in French?
o: Greeting first, using vous when needed, and thanking
Starting with a question about the other person's job
panel.why: The rituals of greeting and thanks are important in French.

teach.model: Start by saying Bonjour or Salut. Ask Ça va? and answer with Ça va bien or Pas mal. Ask back with Et toi? To close say À bientôt or Bonne journée.

stages.hook: Two friends meet on the street. What might they say to each other?
stages.mnemonic: Ça va? Ça va! Et toi? is the first dance of any chat.

trip.prompt: Find which subjects are usually avoided in small talk and note one.
